source_text: Τοῦτο τὸ σχῆμα τὸ βλεπόμενον ἐξαπατᾷ τὸν θάνατον καὶ τὸν διάβολον· ὁ γὰρ ἐντὸς πλοῦτος καὶ τὸ κάλλος αὐτοῖς ἀθέατός ἐστι· καὶ μαίνονται περὶ τὸ σαρκίον, οὗ καταφρονοῦσιν ὡς ἀσθενοῦς. τῶν ἔνδον ὄντες τυφλοὶ κτημάτων, οὐκ ἐπιστάμενοι πηλίκον τινὰ »θησαυρὸν ἐν ὀστρακίνῳ σκεύει« βαστάζομεν, δυνάμει θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ αἵματι θεοῦ παιδὸς καὶ δρόσῳ πνεύματος ἁγίου περιτετειχισμένον. ἀλλὰ σύ γε μὴ ἐξαπατηθῇς. ὁ γεγευμένος ἀληθείας καὶ κατηξιωμένος τῆς μεγάλης λυτρώσεως, ἀλλὰ τὸ ἐναντίον τοῖς ἄλλοις ἀνθρώποις σεαυτῷ κατάλεξον στρατὸν ἄοπλον, ἀπόλεμον, ἀναίμακτον, ἀόργητον, ἀμίαντον, γέροντας θεοσεβεῖς. ὀρφανοὺς θεοφιλεῖς, χήρας πραότητι ὡπλισμένας. ἄνδρας ἀγάπῃ κεκοσμημένους. τοιούτους κτῆσαι τῷ σῷ πλούτῳ καὶ τῷ σώματι καὶ τῇ ψυχῇ δορυφόρους, ὧν στρατηγεῖ θεός. δι᾿ οὓς καὶ ναῦς βαπτιζομένη κουφίζεται, μόναις ἁγίων εὐχαῖς κυβερνωμένη. καὶ νόσος ἀκμάζουσα δαμάζεται, χειρῶν ἐπιβολαῖς διωκομένη. καὶ προσβολὴ λῃστῶν ἀφοπλίζεται, εὐχαῖς εὐσεβέσι σκυλευομένη, καὶ δαιμόνων βία θραύεται προστάγμασι συντόνοις ἐλεγχομένη.
thought_title: The unseen treasure and the army of the poor
orientation: Clement is addressing the rich believer directly, explaining that the visible body deceives death and the devil because the true wealth within is invisible to them, and urging the rich person to enlist the poor and godly as spiritual bodyguards.
pass_a_gloss: This visible shape deceives death and the devil; for the wealth within and the beauty is unseen to them; and they rage around the little flesh, which they despise as weak. Being blind to the possessions within, not knowing how great a treasure in an earthen vessel we carry, walled around by the power of God the Father and the blood of God the child and the dew of the Holy Spirit. But you at least, do not be deceived. You who have tasted truth and been deemed worthy of the great redemption, but on the contrary to the other human beings, enlist for yourself an army unarmed, unwarlike, bloodless, without anger, undefiled, old men who revere God, orphans beloved by God, widows armed with gentleness, men adorned with love. Acquire such as these with your wealth as bodyguards for your body and your soul, over whom God is general. Through whom also a ship being swamped is lightened, steered by the prayers of the saints alone. And a disease at its height is subdued, driven away by the laying on of hands. And an attack of robbers is disarmed, stripped by pious prayers, and the force of demons is shattered, refuted by intense commands.

choices.why: The diminutive σαρκίον is deliberate: death and the devil rage around this small, weak flesh, despising it, while the true wealth within is invisible to them.
This is a direct allusion to 2 Corinthians 4:7, and the glossary term 'treasure' is used for θησαυρός.
The phrase θεοῦ παιδός is unusual and emphatic; rendering it literally as 'God the child' preserves the striking juxtaposition of divine and human.

choices.term: στρατὸν ἄοπλον, ἀπόλεμον, ἀναίμακτον, ἀόργητον, ἀμίαντον
choices.english: an army unarmed, unwarlike, bloodless, without anger, undefiled
choices.why: The string of alpha-privative adjectives is rhetorically important; each is rendered as a single negative adjective to preserve the rhythm and force.
rejected: an army without weapons, without war, without blood, without anger, without stain

choices.why: The military metaphor continues: the poor and godly are to be acquired as δορυφόροι, the spear-bearers or bodyguards who protect a ruler.
βαπτίζω here means 'to be sunk or swamped' in a literal nautical sense, not 'baptized'; the passive participle conveys the ongoing action.

pass_b_english: This visible shape deceives death and the devil, for the wealth within and its beauty are invisible to them. They rage around the little flesh, which they despise as weak. Blind to the possessions within, they do not know what a great treasure in an earthen vessel we carry (2 Corinthians 4:7), walled around by the power of God the Father, the blood of God the child, and the dew of the Holy Spirit. But do not let yourself be deceived. You who have tasted the truth and been deemed worthy of the great redemption—enroll for yourself, in contrast to other people, an army unarmed, unwarlike, bloodless, without anger, undefiled: elders who fear God, orphans beloved of God, widows armed with gentleness, men adorned with love. Acquire such people with your wealth and your body and your soul as bodyguards, over whom God is general. Because of them a ship being swamped is lifted up, steered by the prayers of the holy alone. A raging disease is subdued, driven off by the laying on of hands. An attack of robbers is disarmed, stripped of its spoil by devout prayers. The violence of demons is shattered, convicted by urgent commands.

last_rejected.why: Greek says ‘blood of God the Son’, not ‘child’
last_rejected.ruling: παῖς commonly means 'child' or 'servant'; 'Son' is theological interpretation, not required translation.

last_rejected.quote: they do not know what a great treasure in an earthen vessel we carry
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐκ ἐπιστάμενοι πηλίκον τινὰ «θησαυρὸν ἐν ὀστρακίνῳ σκεύει» βαστάζομεν
last_rejected.why: Verb ‘basτάζομεν’ means ‘we are founded on’, not ‘we carry’; agency is misrepresented
last_rejected.fix: they do not know that a great treasure is held in an earthen vessel, on which we are founded
last_rejected.ruling: βαστάζω standardly means 'carry, bear'; 'founded on' is not its normal range of meaning.

last_rejected.quote: a ship being swamped is lifted up
last_rejected.why: Greek says ‘a ship being baptized is made mute’, not ‘lifted up’
last_rejected.fix: a ship being baptized is made mute
last_rejected.ruling: βαπτίζομαι here means 'swamped/sinking'; κουφίζομαι means 'lightened/lifted up'—translation is correct.

last_rejected.why: Greek means ‘being scourged/whipped’, not ‘stripped of its spoil’
last_rejected.ruling: σκυλεύομαι means 'stripped of arms/spoil'; 'scourged' is σκυλίζω, a different verb.

last_rejected.why: The source specifies ‘commands of the saints’, which is omitted
last_rejected.ruling: προστάγμασι συντόνοις contains no word for 'saints'; 'urgent commands' is accurate.
